newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELKINGTON GRABS FIRST-ROUND LEAD AT PLAYERS CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELKINGTON GRABS FIRST-ROUND LEAD AT PLAYERS CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Australian Steve Elkington rode a hot start on the TPC at Sawgrass course to a one-stroke lead after the first round of the Players Championship on Thursday.
Elkington, who won this tournament in 1991 and three weeks ago won the Doral-Ryder Open, birdied his first four holes en route to a six-under-par 66.
Tom Lehman, Mark Calcavecchia, Fuzzy Zoeller, David Edwards and Russ Cochran were tied for second after each completed the circuit at five-under 67.
A group of 10 more players, including 1987 winner Sandy Lyle of Britain, South African Ernie Els and Larry Mize, were two strokes off the pace on the crowded leader board at 68.
"Obviously I played very well and am pleased with a 66," Elkington said.

"Having won Doral already I felt like it gives me momentum for the rest of this swing. I really prepared myself for this week and I got off to a great start with the four birdies and played steady the rest of the day."
The only blemish on Elkington's round was a double bogey on 18 after he sent a 2-iron second shot into the water.

The win at Doral was his first victory since the 1995 PGA Championship, but Elkington said he did not feel he had been in any kind of prolonged slump. He said his only real setback was the result of having his golf clubs stolen twice in the last 18 months.
"Other than the six months it took me to get over losing my clubs, I feel my game has stayed the same or improved. I still feel very confident," Elkington said.
Zoeller, who shot 20 under par here in 1994 only to lose to Greg Norman's record-breaking 24-under total, said course conditions Thursday were near perfect.
"It was very, very soft out there, and the course is very vulnerable when it's like this. Just a beautiful day to play golf," Zoeller said.
Zoeller carded seven birdies and two bogeys -- not bad for his first tournament round after being sidelined six weeks by a back injury.
"I hurt my back and was out for a month and a half. All I could do was fish," Zoeller said.

Although conditions were perfect and the field featured the top 50 ranked players in the world, the tough TPC course with its treacherous rough made life difficult for anyone who strayed from the fairways.
There were seven scores in the 80's Thursday with three of them coming from former major championship winners -- Australian Wayne Grady (80), Curtis Strange (81) and Ben Crenshaw (81).
Defending champion Fred Couples shot a one-under-par 71, as did pre-tournament favourite Tiger Woods and Masters champion Nick Faldo.
